newsitem.title: FRANCE: French inflation falls for third month in row.
newsitem.headline: French inflation falls for third month in row.

text.p: French consumer prices fell for the third month in a row in August, in what some economists said underlined the weakness in the economy.
National statistics institute INSEE said on Friday consumer prices fell between 0.2 and 0.3 percent in August, giving a year-on-year rise of between 1.6 and 1.7 percent.
"It's a bigger fall than expected. Now inflation has fallen three straight months in a row. It's a little worrying," Jean-Louis Mourier, economist at Louis Dreyfus Finance, said.
"It's not a very positive sign for the economy as it highlights sluggish demand. We're not in a deflation environment, but we are in a weak economy," JP Morgan economist David Naude said.

The fall in prices was partly due to the fact that a rise last August in Value Added Tax (sales tax) was no longer playing a role, although economists said the slowdown was due to more than just this factor.
"There is a slowdown in underlying inflation," Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP) economist Philippe Cheval said.
News of the latest fall in inflation however delighted the bond market, which rose on hopes of a new cut in interest rates.
"It's weaker than expected. It confirms that there is no inflation in France and we now expect further easing on rates," Nathalie Fillet, bond analyst at Banque Paribas, said.
